# Command-line reference

<!-- generated by docs/gen_cli.py from interfacer.cli.build_parser; do not edit by hand -->

`interfacer [options]` and `python interfacer-new.py [options]` take the same options.
Every option except `--input`, `--save_input`, `--help` and `--version` can also go in an input file (see [Input files](input_files.md)); the file key is the long name without dashes (e.g. `convSep`) or the short name (e.g. `tsep`).


## Input and output

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-i1`, `--infile1` |  | Bulk structure of material 1 (bottom slab); any format ASE can read (cif, POSCAR, res, xyz, ...). |
| `-i2`, `--infile2` |  | Bulk structure of material 2 (top slab); required unless --gb is used. |
| `-i3`, `--infile3` |  | Bulk structure of material 3 for three-layer interfaces slab1\|slab2\|slab3 (optional). |
| `-o`, `--outfile` | `interfaces.out` | Summary file with the surface energies and works of adhesion. Def: interfaces.out |
| `-m1`, `--miller1` | `1 0 0` | Miller indices of the surface of material 1, e.g. -m1 1 1 0. Def: 1 0 0 |
| `-m2`, `--miller2` | `1 0 0` | Miller indices of the surface of material 2. Def: 1 0 0 |
| `-m3`, `--miller3` | `1 0 0` | Miller indices of the surface of material 3 (-i3). Def: 1 0 0 |
| `-cr3`, `--creps3` |  | Repetitions in c direction (number of layers) for surface model 3 (-i3). Def: 1 |
| `-sep2`, `--sep2` |  | Separation between slab 2 and slab 3 in three-layer interfaces (A). Def: -sep |
| `--gb` {tilt,twist} |  | Grain-boundary mode: a symmetric tilt or a twist boundary of material 1 (-i1) with the boundary plane -m1, instead of an interface of two materials. |
| `--gb_mn` | `2 1` | CSL integers m n of a twist boundary (square or hexagonal planes), e.g. 2 1 for Sigma5 on cubic (100) or Sigma7 on fcc (111). Def: 2 1 |
| `--gb_expansion` |  | Extra rigid-body separation at each symmetric tilt boundary (A). Def: 0 |
| `-surf1`, `--surface1` |  | extra input file for a surface structure of i1 |
| `-surf2`, `--surface2` |  | extra input file for a surface structure of i2 |

## Slabs and interfaces

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-cr1`, `--creps1` |  | Repetitions in c direction (number of layers) for surface model 1 |
| `-cr2`, `--creps2` |  | Repetitions in c direction (number of layers) for surface model 2 |
| `-msd`, `--max_slab_dimension` | `50` | Maximum length (A) of the in-plane cell vectors in the search for a commensurate supercell. Def: 50 A |
| `-th`, `--thickness` | `7` | Minimum thickness of the symmetric slabs (-sym_slabs1/2), def: 7A. The thickness of the other slabs is set by -cr1/-cr2. |
| `-pt`, `--percentage_tolerance` | `4` | Tolerance (%%) for matching the in-plane angles and lengths of the two slabs (i.e. the maximum strain). Def: 4 |
| `-Linit`, `--initLength` | `3` | Initial (minimum) length of surface slabs in a/b direction, def: 3A |
| `-Lstep`, `--stepLength` | `2` | step size for the increasing the length in a/b direction, def: 2A |
| `-vac_slab`, `--vac_slab` | `6.0` | Size of vacuum padding in z direction (only for slabs), def: 6 A on both sites |
| `-vac_int`, `--vac_int` | `1.0` | Size of vacuum padding in z direction (only for interface), def: 1.0 A on both sites |
| `-sep`, `--sep` | `2.0` | Seperation between the surface slabs forming the interface, def: 2.0 A |
| `-pass`, `--pas` |  | To passivate the top and bottom surface of the interface slab based on dangling bonds. |
| `-prim`, `--prim` |  | Use primitive cell for bulk 1 and 2. Def: no |
| `-niggli`, `--niggli` |  | Niggli reduce the resulting interface. Def: no |
| `-flip2`, `--flip2` |  | Flip the slab2 upside-down. |
| `-sym_slabs1`, `--symSlabs1` |  | Create symmetric surface slabs for infile1. Def: no |
| `--sym_method` {pymatgen,internal} | `pymatgen` | Generator of the symmetric slabs (-sym_slabs1/2): pymatgen's SlabGenerator or INTERFACER's own implementation. Def: pymatgen |
| `-sym_slabs2`, `--symSlabs2` |  | Create symmetric surface slabs for infile2. Def: no |
| `-no_slabs`, `--noSlabs` | `1` | Number of slabs to be used for interface creation, starting from the most stable slab. Def: 1 |
| `-cp1`, `--chem_pots1` |  | Chemical potentials for the slab1, e.g. "{'Fe':-3.0, 'O':-2.0}" (in eV). Def: No |
| `-cp2`, `--chem_pots2` |  | Chemical potentials for the slab2, e.g. "{'Fe':-3.0, 'O':-2.0}" (in eV). Def: No |
| `-decomps1`, `--decomps1` |  | list of decomposition structure files of slab1. Def: No |
| `-decomps2`, `--decomps2` |  | list of decomposition structure files of slab2. Def: No |
| `--sfe_scan1` |  | SFE of all slabs of material 1 vs the chemical potential of one element, e.g. 'Na,Cl,-1.0,0.0': Delta mu(Na) from -1 to 0 eV relative to the reference chemical potentials (-cp1/-decomps1), compensated by Cl to keep the bulk in equilibrium. Writes OUTPUT/sfe_vs_mu_1.csv/.png. Def: none |
| `--sfe_scan2` |  | As --sfe_scan1 for material 2. Def: none |
| `-surf_only`, `--surf_only` |  | Use to only calculate the surfaces and exit before the creation of the interfaces. Def: no |

## Convergence and screening tests

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-tsur`, `-test_surf`, `--checkSurfs` |  | To check the stability of different surfaces for the given materials. Def: No |
| `-tlay`, `-test_layer`, `--convLayers` |  | To run a convergence test on the layer thickness for slab(s) generated. Def: No |
| `-tsep`, `-test_sep`, `--convSep` |  | To run a convergence test on the interlayer separation for the interface generated. Def: No |
| `-thor`, `-test_hori`, `--test_hori` |  | To run a convergence test on the relative placement of slabs w.r.t. each other for the interface generated. Def: No |
| `-topt`, `--test_opt` |  | Optimise the placement of the rigid slabs (lateral shift and separation) with scipy on single-point energies, starting from the best -thor/-tsep result. Def: No |
| `--topt_maxiter` | `60` | Maximum number of iterations of -topt. Def: 60 |
| `--minkowski` |  | 2D Minkowski (Gauss) reduction of the matched in-plane cell of the aligned slabs/interface. Def: No |
| `-mlist`, `--miller_list` | `100 010 001 110 111` | list of Miller indices to check during the surface stability analysis (--checkSurfs), e.g. -mlist 100 110 111 or -mlist 1,0,0 1,-1,0. Def: 100 010 001 110 111 |
| `-sep_init`, `--sep_init` | `1.0` | Initial interface separation to be used in seperation convergence test (--convSep), def: 1.0 A |
| `-sep_final`, `--sep_final` | `3.0` | Final interface separation (included) to be used in seperation convergence test (--convSep), def: 3.0 A |
| `-sep_step`, `--sep_step` | `0.25` | Step size in interface separation to be used in seperation convergence test (--convSep), def: 0.25 A |
| `-lay_min`, `--lay_min` | `2` | Min layers to include n layer thickness convergence test (--convLay), def: 2 layers |
| `-lay_max`, `--lay_max` | `8` | Max layers to include n layer thickness convergence test (--convLay), def: 8 layers |
| `-hor_steps`, `--hor_steps` | `0.25 0.25` | Horizontal translations (relative to lattice vectors) of bottom layer in x and y directions for slab placement test (--test_hori), def: [0.25, 0.25]] |

## Calculation settings

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-prog`, `--prog` {castep,vasp,ase,mlip,gpaw,onetep} |  | Code to be used: CASTEP, VASP, ASE (simple LJ/Morse/EMT potentials, see -ase_pot), MLIP (machine-learning potentials, see --mlip), GPAW or ONETEP (through ASE, see --calc_kwargs) |
| `-xc`, `--xc` | `PBE` | Exchange correlation functional to use (pseudopots will be selected accordingly, e.g. LDA, PBE,PBEsol, etc. Def: PBE |
| `-ec`, `--encut` | `520` | Cutoff energy for the planewaves Def: 520 eV |
| `-kp_sp`, `--kpspacing` | `0.32` | KP grid spacing, Def: 0.05 * 2 pi = 0.32 1/A |
| `-kp_gr`, `--kpgrid` |  | KP grid dimensions for the slabs and interfaces, e.g. '4 4 1' (Using KP spacing is recommended), Def: None |
| `-gamma`, `--gamma_only` |  | Set KP grid to 1 1 1 and use only the Gamma point for surface slabs and interface. This switches on the gamma_only version of VASP. |
| `-sig`, `--sigma` | `0.05` | Gaussian smearing width, Def:0.05 eV |
| `-mgm`, `--magmoms` |  | Magnetic moments for a collinear calculation. Eg, 'Fe 5.0 Nb 0.6 O 0.6' Def.: None. If a defined element is not present in the POSCAR, no MAGMOM will be set for it. |
| `-hubU`, `--hubU` |  | For defining the Hubbard U parameters (in eV) for specific atom and orbital types, e.g. -hubU Fe d 2.7, Sm f 6.1 |
| `-ase_pot`, `--ase_pot` {LJ,Morse,EMT} | `LJ` | Potential type to be used through the ASE infrastructure, only relevant when using -prog 'ASE'. Def: LJ |
| `-ase_fmax`, `--ase_fmax` | `0.05` | Force convergence criterion when using the ASE built-in geometry optimiser. Def: 0.05 eV/A |
| `-ase_gsteps`, `--ase_gsteps` | `200` | Max number of BFGS steps allowed in the ASE built-in geometry optimiser. Def: 200 geometry steps |
| `-mp`, `-makepotcar`, `--makepotcar` |  | to compile POTCAR (for VASP) using actual atomic content. The environment variable ($VASP_PP_PATH) should be defined beforehand. Default: False. |
| `--potcarxc` | `potpaw_PBE` | XC functional to use in making of POTCAR. Def: potpaw_PBE |
| `-cparam`, `--castep_param` | `input.param` | CASTEP parameter file to read (optional). Def: input.param |
| `-ccell`, `--castep_cell` | `input.cell` | CASTEP cell file to read (optional). Def: input.cell |
| `-cpp`, `--castep_PP` | `OTF` | CASTEP pseudopotential (PP, options are OTF, 00PBE, etc.). Def: OTF |

## Parallelisation (VASP/CASTEP)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-np`, `--nprocs` | `32` | No of processes to start for each CASTEP/VASP calculation through srun/mpirun. Def:32 |
| `-nt`, `--ntasks` | `1` | No of CASTEP/VASP tasks to run simultaneously. Def:1 |
| `-nn`, `--nnodes` | `1` | No of nodes to run CASTEP/VASP runs through srun. Def:1 |
| `-mpi`, `--mpirun` |  | Use mpirun for parallel runs. Default: srun is used |
| `-vexe`, `--vexe` | `vasp_std` | Vasp exectuable. Def: vasp_std |
| `-mpiargs`, `--mpiargs` |  | Extra arguments for srun/mpirun, e.g. "--partition=<name>". No default value. |

## General

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-dry`, `--dry`, `--structures_only` |  | Dry run / structures only: build and write all structures (and VASP/CASTEP inputs) without running any calculation, for all codes. Good for checking the slabs and the interfacing algorithm. |
| `-view`, `--view` |  | To view the generated structures. |
| `-v`, `--verb` |  | Verbose output: also show details (supercell search, optimiser steps, passivation, ...). Default: False. |
| `-q`, `--quiet` |  | Only show warnings and errors. Default: False. |
| `-quick`, `--quick` |  | Setup a quick test run using ASE/LJ potentials to check functionality. Default: False. |

## ASE optimiser (-prog ase / mlip)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--optimiser`, `--ase_opt` {BFGS,FIRE,LBFGS} | `BFGS` | ASE optimiser for the ASE-based engines. Def: BFGS |
| `--relax_cell_bulk` |  | ASE/MLIP engines: also relax the cell of the bulk structures (and decomposition products). Def: yes for -prog mlip, no for -prog ase (VASP/CASTEP always relax the bulk cell) |
| `--no_relax_cell_bulk` |  | ASE/MLIP engines: keep the cell of the bulk structures fixed. |

## Machine-learning potentials (-prog mlip)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--mlip` | `mace` | Machine-learning potential for -prog mlip: mace, mace-off, chgnet, matgl, sevennet, orb, fairchem, nequip, allegro, or custom:package.module:function (any function returning an ASE calculator). Def: mace |
| `--mlip_model` |  | Model name or path for --mlip, e.g. 'medium-mpa-0' or 'my.model' (MACE), '7net-0' (SevenNet), 'uma-s-1' (fairchem). Def: the backend default |
| `--device` | `auto` | Device for the machine-learning potential: cpu, cuda, mps or auto. Def: auto (GPU if available) |
| `--mlip_kwargs` |  | Extra keyword arguments for the ML potential calculator as a Python dict, e.g. "{'default_dtype': 'float32'}" or "{'task_name': 'omat'}". Def: none |
| `--fix_mode` {bottom,middle} | `bottom` | Which layers --fix_layers keeps fixed: the lowest ones or the central (bulk-like) ones. Def: bottom |
| `--calc_kwargs` |  | Extra settings for -prog gpaw/onetep as a Python dict, e.g. "{'spinpol': True}" (GPAW) or "{'keywords': {'maxit_ngwf_cg': 50}, 'ngwfs_radius': 8.0}" (ONETEP). Def: none |
| `--fix_layers` |  | Keep the lowest N atomic layers of the slabs fixed in the slab optimisations (bulk-like region). Def: 0 |
| `--restart` |  | Reuse finished calculations, also of the convergence tests (VASP/CASTEP: default; ASE/MLIP: results are kept in ASE-calcs/ and reused if the input structure and settings are unchanged). |
| `--overwrite` |  | Redo all calculations; existing VASP run directories and CASTEP outputs are moved to *_old<n> (not deleted). |
| `--outdir` | `OUTPUT` | Directory for the output structures (the previous one is kept as <outdir>_prev). Def: OUTPUT |
| `--version` | `==SUPPRESS==` | show program's version number and exit |

## Input files

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--input`, `-inp` |  | Input file (TOML, YAML or JSON) with options; keys are the long option names (e.g. infile1, miller1, prog, convSep). Options given on the command line override the file. |
| `--save_input` |  | Write the effective options of this run to a TOML/YAML/JSON file (by extension) that can be used with --input. |
